Nothing is ever deleted, which is the point (an assessment must be able to resolve a citation however old), and nothing bounds the growth either. `helena.enrichment.prune_snapshots` is the shape it would take; what it may keep is a function of how far back replay has to reach, which concept/08 still lists as open.

A SHORTER RETENTION FOR NEGATIVES than for hits. The argument is real — an unlisted indicator may be listed tomorrow, while a listing rarely disappears — and it is unmeasured. One retention per (source, endpoint), applied to both.

THE DISCLOSURE RECORD (task 37). The log line carries `disclosed` per call and that is a local log line, not the disclosure row concept/03 asks for. The response table already stores the indicator as asked, which is the string that row has to name.
BUDGET ENFORCEMENT (task 36). A cache hit already costs no live query and nothing counts either number.

THE ANALYST TIER IN THE ENRICHED CONTEXT. helena_reference_evidence_analyst is deliberately NOT unioned into helena_reference_evidence: the tier tag would keep analyst rows out of the triage rendering, but they would still enter the enriched context of every later host that talked to the same address, which concept/03 names as the outcome the tag exists to prevent rather than one it makes safe. How an analyst claim reaches a finding is the findings increment's; the view is where it attaches.
IDN FOLDING in the cache key, and a `mailto:`-shaped (non-hierarchical) URI. Both are left unfolded on purpose — see the normalization rule — and IDN needs a dependency this project does not have.

RETENTION AS CONFIGURATION FILE VALUES. `retention_seconds` is a required constructor argument, so it is configured per (source, endpoint) by whoever builds the tool. The real numbers cannot be written yet: no live endpoint exists, and a value written from a documentation page is the error this project has corrected three times. config/*.toml is where they land when task 38 confirms the surface.
35.makes_buildable: Task 36 (budgets) has the two counters it needs already separated at the boundary: a cache hit costs a step and no live query, and `ProviderTool.lookup` is still the only place a provider is reached. Task 37 (send policy and the disclosure record) has the exact point where a disclosure row goes — the log already carries `disclosed` per call, true on a live query, false on a hit, true on a stale fallback — and `helena_reference_analyst_response` already stores the indicator AS ASKED beside the normalized key, which is the literal string a disclosure record has to name. Task 38 (the live adapter) is unchanged behind `ask(call, credential)` and now gets replay for free: the first pass spends the quota, every re-run reads the stored bytes. Task 39 (the analyst loop) gets a `ToolAnswer` whose steps already carry `cache_hit`/`live_query` and the underlying record's retrieval time, which is what a gap of kind `stale` is derived from. The increment that joins an analyst-tier claim to a finding attaches at `helena_reference_evidence_analyst`.
35.next_session_should_know: Task 36 is budgets and this task built the thing budgets are counted over. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS NOW `ProviderTool(source_id=..., endpoint='<logical-name>', credential=..., ask=<adapter>, cache=EvidenceCache(connection), retention_seconds=<int>, logger=..., redactor=...)`. `endpoint` and `retention_seconds` are required and have no defaults, `endpoint` must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_]*$ (it reaches the tool name the model is shown, so it is not a path and never a URL), and the tool's name is now `lookup_<source>_<endpoint>`. (2) A CACHE HIT COSTS A STEP AND NO LIVE QUERY, which is the distinction concept/07 says the two budgets have to be set against each other over — 'a budget that seems generous for a model call is not survivable for a handful of provider lookups'. The two numbers are countable off `RetrievalStep.outcome` without adding anything. (3) THE STALE FALLBACK IS AN ANSWER WITH TWO STEPS AND ONE OF THEM IS A FAILURE. Anything that walks `ToolAnswer.steps` assuming a failure means no evidence is wrong now; `ToolAnswer.failure` still returns the typed error and `record.status` is `stale` on every served row. (4) `missing` STILL HAS NO PRODUCER AT THIS LAYER AND MUST NOT GET ONE FROM A CACHE MISS. A miss is the reason to query, not an absence of a source; recording it as `missing` is the collapse concept/instruction.md §2 forbids wearing an optimisation's clothes. (5) TESTS/TEST_TOOLS.PY IS AN INTEGRATION MODULE NOW. `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration`, an autouse `_store` fixture takes `migrated_engine` and pushes it onto `_ENGINE`, and `cache()`/`tool()` read it. If you add a test there it gets an engine whether it wants one or not. (6) NOTHING IS EVICTED AND NOTHING PRUNES. Both cache tables grow without bound, on purpose (see docs/decisions/0025 §1) and with no bound. If a later increment wants one, the shape is `enrichment.prune_snapshots` and the retention horizon is an open question in concept/08, not a number to pick. (7) THE STAND-IN ADAPTER STILL CLAIMS NOTHING ABOUT THE HUNTING API'S ENVELOPE. That is still task 38's to confirm against the artifact, and it is still the mistake concept/05 records most emphatically.
35.summary: `ProviderTool.lookup` is cache-first: it reads a valid, unexpired record for its source, endpoint and normalized indicator out of the one store and returns it without touching the network, querying only on a miss or an expiry. The cache is the evidence store and not a second one — `sql/migrations/0017_analyst_lookup_cache.sql` adds two tables and a view in the streaming engine, in the evidence shape 0011 defined, and nothing is ever evicted. `helena.enrichment.ANALYST_TIER` now has a SQL home and a duplicated-constant test that asks the engine.
35.title: [D5 Tools] Cache-first lookup where the cache is the evidence store

deferred: PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. `config/policy.toml`'s `[rate_limits]` is read for the derivation and nothing sleeps between calls, so the rate the tool layer 'holds itself to' is not yet a rate it enforces in time. The live adapter (task 38) is where a throttle belongs — it is the only thing that knows a request left the process — and the wall-clock budget already charges the wait when it happens. Stated in the module docstring, the config file and README rather than implied.

A MEASURED PROVIDER RATE LIMIT. `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is a self-imposed ceiling, not a measurement: abuse.ch publishes fair-use terms rather than a number, and measuring one would mean deliberately exceeding it against a live service. `concept/07`'s own 'a few lookups per minute' is the shape it comes from, and it must be lowered the moment a provider states less.

EVERY NUMBER IN `[budgets.*]` IS A CANDIDATE. No per-run token consumption has been measured, no provider latency distribution exists, and `concept/08` still lists the numeric budget values as open. What is demonstrated is that they are loaded from the file, enforced at the boundary, and changeable without touching code — the same standing the 0.80 threshold and `config/agents.toml`'s 3 have.

`budgets_version`. Deliberately NOT added to `config/policy.toml`: `thresholds_version` exists because an `Escalation` records it, and nothing records a budget version — no assessment row exists and `Budgets` has no version field. A key nothing reads is what the rest of that file refuses. Task 43 adds it with the column that reads it.

SERVING AN EXPIRED RECORD WHEN THE LIVE-QUERY BUDGET IS SPENT. The call is refused instead, and the choice is argued in ADR-0026 §3: the stale fallback exists because the PROVIDER did not answer, and letting a budget decide what the evidence is would make two runs differing only in budget differ in what they cite. If a later increment wants the other behaviour it is a change to this decision, not an optimisation.

NOTHING STORES A `Cost`, so 'budgets consumed, latency and tokens are recorded on the assessment' is a ready shape and not a property that holds. `RunBudget.cost()` produces the record; task 43 stores it.

NO AGENT HAS BEEN BUDGETED THROUGH A TOOL LOOP, because no analyst loop exists (task 39). Every dimension is enforced and tested at the boundary it is enforced at, and nothing has yet driven all four in one run of a real agent.

`degraded` HAS NO CALLER IN THE TREE. `helena.triage.run` deliberately does not call it — a triage `AgentResult` can never come back from a ledger that refused something (the only guards on that path are `check_tokens`, which ends the run with a failure, and the clock, which is `timed_out`), so calling it there would be dead code that could only ever raise. The analyst runner is its caller.
36.makes_buildable: Task 39 (the analyst tool loop) gets the object the loop is bounded by and the two calls it makes: `budget = RunBudget.of(request)` once, then `tool.lookup(arguments, scope=..., budget=budget)` per turn and `assess(request, ..., budget=budget)` per model call, with `degraded(outcome, budget)` at the end. It needs no budget arithmetic of its own and cannot accidentally get a fresh clock. Task 37 (send policy and disclosure) has the refusal vocabulary it extends — `REFUSAL_REASONS` is now three — and the place its check goes is the same dispatch, after the budget and before the cache read. Task 38 (the live adapter) has the number it must pace itself to (`config/policy.toml`'s `[rate_limits]`) and the guard that catches it when it does not: provider waits are on the run's clock. Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets `RunBudget.cost(retries=...)` as the row's budgets-consumed, latency, tokens and cache-hit-versus-live-query columns, and owes the two things named in the escalations: the monetary column with the price table it is derived from, and a `budgets_version` if it wants to record which budget policy governed a run.
36.next_session_should_know: Task 37 is the disclosure record and the send policy, and the dispatch it edits now has a budget in front of it. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `tool.lookup(arguments, scope=RunScope.of(request), budget=RunBudget.of(request), now=...)`. `budget` is keyword-only with no default, exactly like `scope`, and for the same reason — there is no argument a model could put one in and no way for a caller to omit one and still get a lookup. `helena.agents.assess` takes the same object under the same rules. (2) THE CHARGE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND YOUR CHECK GOES AFTER IT: a step and the clock first (so a malformed call still costs a turn of the loop), then argument validation, then the entity-type check, then the cache read, then the live query. A send-policy refusal belongs between validation and the cache read, and it costs a step and no live query — `REFUSAL_REASONS` is now `(malformed_arguments, entity_type_not_covered, budget_exhausted)` and `tools.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` IS `contract.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, imported rather than respelled. (3) A CACHE HIT ANSWERS AFTER THE QUOTA IS SPENT. That is deliberate and tested: the live query is charged after the cache read. Do not move a check that could refuse the call to before the cache read unless you mean 'this run may not read what it already fetched' — which is what the wall-clock check does mean. (4) `exhausted` MEANS REFUSED, NOT SPENT. `RunBudget.gap()` returns the `budget_exhausted` gap only when the run asked for more of something and could not have it; a run that spent its last token on the answer it returned is a run that finished. `degraded(outcome, budget)` is the only place code rewrites a classification, it re-validates through the contract, and it RAISES for a triage `normal` because triage has no `unknown` root. (5) THE VALUES ARE IN `config/policy.toml` NOW, IN TWO NEW TABLES, AND `live_queries` IS NOT A KEY — it is derived from `retrieval_seconds` and the slowest `[rate_limits]` entry, and the loader refuses a pair that contradicts itself. `helena.policy.THRESHOLD_KEYS` and `BUDGET_KEYS` are why both loaders still start on that file; add a key to neither loader's set and it will be refused, which is the intended behaviour. (6) `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` IS SELF-IMPOSED AND NOT MEASURED, and NOTHING PACES CALLS TO IT. If task 38 confirms a published limit, that number moves and the derived live-query budget moves with it; if you add a throttle, the wall-clock budget is already charging the wait. (7) THE FULL SUITE IS 1 289 TESTS IN ~295 s ON THIS MACHINE, NO SKIPS. `tests/test_budgets.py` needs no engine (the ledger is arithmetic over an injected `Clock`); the budget tests in `tests/test_tools.py` do, because that whole module is integration, and `ledger()`/`driven()` there are the helpers to reuse.
36.summary: `helena.budgets` is the budget guard: `RunBudget` is one ledger per agent run carrying the four dimensions from `AgentRequest.budgets` and what has been spent of each, and both `helena.agents.assess` and `helena.tools.ProviderTool.lookup` now take it keyword-only with no default and charge the same object — so the wall clock covers the whole run including provider waits, steps and live queries are refused inside the dispatch rather than discouraged in a prompt, and a spent dimension is a typed `ToolRefusal` carrying `budget_exhausted`. The values are loaded from `config/policy.toml` beside the thresholds, the live-query count is derived from the retrieval allowance and the slowest configured provider rate rather than configured, and `budgets.degraded` turns a truncated `normal` analyst verdict into `unknown` with the exhaustion explicit, through the contract's own validation.
36.title: [D5 Tools] Budget guards enforced at the tool boundary

deferred: STORING A DISCLOSURE ROW. The ledger is in-process and ephemeral; `concept/07` allows that of working memory and requires the record on the assessment, which task 43 owes. Until then a run's disclosures are lost when the process ends — the one thing an auditor would actually want.

WHETHER AN INDICATOR THE MODEL INVENTED MAY BE SENT AT ALL. Still the sharpest gap the tool layer leaves, and the send policy does not close it: the policy governs what KINDS of thing and WHICH FIELDS may be sent and never asks where the value came from. Closing it needs the host context beside the tool, which is the analyst runner's shape rather than this layer's. Named in `helena.tools`' 'deliberately not here' section and in ADR-0027 §6.

GOVERNING THE MODEL CHANNEL PER FIELD. What of a context reaches a prompt is the rendering's decision under a recorded `rendering_version`, and a second field list in the send policy would be a second opinion about it. What this increment adds for that channel is the record, not a second gate.

VERIFYING THAT AN ADAPTER SPEAKS TO `disclosed_to`. `helena.tools` holds no URL at all (asserted off its own AST), so the layer could not check the request even in principle. It becomes checkable when a live adapter exists (task 38).
PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from task 36: `[rate_limits]` is read for the live-query derivation and nothing sleeps between calls.
37.makes_buildable: Task 38 (the live adapter) has the host its requests must go to, in policy rather than in code (`send_policy.threatfox.disclosed_to = threatfox-api.abuse.ch`, re-measured 2026-09-09: 401 without the `Auth-Key` header, no credential and no indicator sent), and the guarantee that whatever it builds a body from is the `ToolCall` and nothing else. Task 39 (the analyst loop) builds `Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy())` once beside `RunBudget.of(request)` and threads both through `tool.lookup(..., budget=..., disclosures=...)` and `assess(..., budget=..., disclosures=...)`; `ProviderTool.declaration()` now offers the intersection of what the source covers and what the policy permits, so the loop cannot be handed a tool that invites refusals. Task 41 (replay) gets the counting rule it needs — a run's disclosures are its live queries, and a full replay must therefore record none. Task 42 (orchestration) is the code that owns the ledger: `helena.triage.run` takes it and does not build it. Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets `Disclosures.rows` as the column to store, beside `RunBudget.cost`, and owes both.
37.next_session_should_know: Task 38 is the first live provider tool and this task built the two things that decide what it may send and what gets recorded. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS NOW `ProviderTool(source_id=..., endpoint=..., credential=..., ask=..., cache=..., retention_seconds=..., send_policy=<SendPolicy>, logger=..., redactor=...)` and `tool.lookup(arguments, scope=RunScope.of(request), budget=RunBudget.of(request), disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy()), now=...)`. All four keyword arguments are required and none has a default. `helena.agents.assess` and `helena.triage.run` take `disclosures` on the same terms. (2) A TOOL FOR A SOURCE WITH NO `[send_policy.<source>]` ENTRY CANNOT BE BUILT — `sslbl-ja3` has none, deliberately, because it is a feed the loader copies locally and a local join discloses nothing. An entry means the source may be QUERIED LIVE, which is the same condition `[rate_limits]` states of itself; a live adapter for a new source needs both. (3) THE HOST IS IN POLICY AND NOT IN CODE. `disclosed_to = "threatfox-api.abuse.ch"`, and the loader refuses anything that is not a bare host. `helena.tools` still imports no HTTP machinery and holds no `://` literal, asserted off its own AST — the adapter is where the protocol lives, and the URL it builds is the adapter's own. (4) THE ADAPTER SEAM IS UNCHANGED: `ask(call: ToolCall, credential: Secret) -> ProviderAnswer`. That is deliberate and it is what makes the field policy structural — the `ToolCall` is the only thing an adapter has to build a body from, so a field the policy withholds is a request that cannot exist. If you need to send more than the indicator, add the field to `ToolCall`, add it to `helena.disclosure.SENDABLE_FIELDS` (a test asserts the two sets are equal), and permit it in the file — in that order, or the tool refuses every call. (5) A CACHE HIT RECORDS NO DISCLOSURE AND THE COUNTS RECONCILE: `len(disclosures.to_channel(PROVIDER_LOOKUP)) == budget.live_queries_spent`. If you add a path that reaches a provider, it charges the live query AND records the row, or that assertion in tests/test_tools.py fails — which is the intended way to find out. (6) THE LEDGER IS IN MEMORY AND NOTHING STORES IT. `Disclosures.rows` is the column task 43 owes, beside `RunBudget.cost`; until then the record dies with the process, and the README and ADR-0027 §6 both say so. Do not 'fix' this with a table without reading ADR-0027 §6 first — it is the same deferral `Cost` has. (7) `config/policy.toml` NOW HAS THREE TABLES AND THREE LOADERS. A bare key appended at the foot of that file lands inside `[rate_limits]`; version keys go at the top. If you add a fourth table, add its key set to `helena.policy` beside the other three or the existing loaders will refuse the file.
37.summary: `helena.disclosure` is the two halves of `concept/07`'s privacy sentence: `SendPolicy` is a per-source whitelist loaded from `config/policy.toml` — the host its requests go to, which entity types this deployment permits being disclosed to it, and which fields of the outbound request may be populated — and `Disclosures` is one ledger per agent run holding one typed `Disclosure` per outbound call. `helena.tools.ProviderTool` resolves a permission at construction (so a tool for a source no policy permits cannot be built), enforces it before the cache is read, refuses with a fourth typed reason `send_policy_forbids` rather than trimming, and records the disclosure before the adapter is called. `helena.agents.assess` records a model call on the same footing, once per attempt, because inference is hosted.
37.title: [D5 Tools] Disclosure recording and send policy

deferred: THE PUBLISHER'S FALSE-POSITIVE LIST, AND IT IS DEFERRED FOR ABSENCE OF THE ARTIFACT RATHER THAN FOR EFFORT. Measured 2026-09-10: ThreatFox publishes no FP feed on either surface this project can reach — the documented operation set has none, `get_fp`/`fp_list`/`false_positives` each answered `unknown_operation`, and the export offers JSON, CSV, MISP, RPZ, host-file and Suricata and no FP file. What the publisher does instead is EXPIRE IOCs older than six months, and an expired IOC is simply absent from both surfaces, which is a deletion — precisely the mechanism `concept/05` says a suppression must not be. The design the task asks for is written in full in ADR-0028 §8 and in `concept/05`: a claim is never deleted and keeps its evidence id, suppression is a SECOND CLAIM from its own source at its own tier rather than a column on the one it suppresses, what a suppressing claim DOES is a named rule in a frozen `helena.policy.vN`, a suppressed match is still shown by the rendering and the assessment, and absence from an FP list is not a clearance. Writing the code would have meant inventing the artifact it consumes, which is the failure mode this whole increment exists to avoid.

PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from tasks 36 and 37, and this module is now the right home for it — it is the only thing that knows a request left the process. `config/policy.toml`'s `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is still self-imposed: abuse.ch publishes fair-use terms and no number, no rate-limit header appears on any response, and measuring one would mean deliberately exceeding it against a live service. The wall-clock budget charges the wait when it happens.

A SECOND PROVIDER. VirusTotal stays deferred by `concept/05` with a narrow role and a shared daily quota, and its adapter would be the second user that would justify any abstraction here. Nothing was built for it.

AGGREGATOR ORIGIN RETENTION (`concept/05` rule 7). Unchanged: `ProviderClaim` has no origin field, `EnrichmentEvidence` has no column, and ThreatFox is not an aggregator. The first aggregator tool owes both.
STORING THE DISCLOSURE ROW AND THE `Cost`. Unchanged from tasks 36-37: the ledgers are in-process and task 43 owes the columns.

THE RETENTION AS A MEASURED NUMBER. It is DERIVED — `SourceDescriptor.refresh_interval_seconds`, 3 600 s, the publisher's own fetch floor — on the rule that an answer stays valid for as long as this deployment would be willing to ask again. That is a rule rather than a picked number, but no hit rate and no staleness cost has been measured and `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open. Task 35 said the real numbers land in `config/*.toml` once the surface is confirmed; a key there today would be a key nothing reads, since `threatfox_tool` derives it and nothing else builds a live tool.

A WHOLE AGENT RUN. No analyst loop exists (task 39), so nothing has driven this tool from a model's tool call, and no budget has been spent across a real multi-lookup run. The maturity label on both `helena.providers` and `helena.tools` says `experimental` and says exactly this.
38.makes_buildable: Task 39 (the analyst tool loop) has a working live tool in one call: `providers.threatfox_tool(credential=settings.providers.abusech_auth_key, cache=EvidenceCache(connection), send_policy=send_policy(), logger=..., redactor=..., timeout_seconds=...)` returns a `ProviderTool` with the source, the endpoint (`search_ioc`), the host (from policy) and the retention (derived from the descriptor's 3 600 s refresh floor) all resolved — the loop supplies only `scope`, `budget`, `disclosures` and `now`. Task 41 (replay) gets what it needs for free: the first pass spends the quota and stores the bytes under their digest, every re-run reads them. Task 43 (assessment persistence) gets a real `native_evidence` shape to store, including `records_returned`/`records_out_of_scope`, which is the count that makes 'the provider listed nothing' and 'the provider listed things about other entities' two different rows. Anything reading analyst claims now has a measured reason to treat ThreatFox-analyst-agreeing-with-ThreatFox-enrichment as one source, not two.
38.next_session_should_know: Task 39 is the analyst tool loop and it now has a real provider to drive. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE WHOLE TOOL IS ONE CALL: `providers.threatfox_tool(credential=settings.providers.abusech_auth_key, cache=tools.EvidenceCache(connection), send_policy=disclosure.send_policy(), logger=..., redactor=..., timeout_seconds=...)`. Everything provider-specific is DERIVED and not passed — the host from `[send_policy.threatfox] disclosed_to`, the endpoint from `providers.SEARCH_IOC`, the retention from the descriptor's 3 600 s refresh floor — so the loop supplies only `scope=RunScope.of(request)`, `budget=RunBudget.of(request)`, `disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy())` and `now`. The tool's name is `lookup_threatfox_search_ioc`. (2) `timeout_seconds` HAS NO DEFAULT AND IT IS NOT THE RUN'S CLOCK. It bounds ONE request; `RunBudget`'s wall clock bounds the analysis and is charged on the same ledger as the model calls. A request that outlives the first is a `timeout` QueryFailure; a run that outlives the second is a `budget_exhausted` ToolRefusal with nothing queried. Pick it from `config/policy.toml`'s `[budgets.analyst] retrieval_seconds` divided by the live-query budget, or say why not. (3) A `no_match` FROM THIS TOOL MAY MEAN TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE COUNTS SAY WHICH. `native_evidence` carries `records_returned` and `records_out_of_scope`: `(0, 0)` is 'the provider listed nothing', `(n, n)` is 'the provider listed n things, none about this indicator' — which happens whenever a wildcard address query hits a URL containing that address. Anything summarising analyst evidence should not flatten those into one sentence. (4) NOTHING PACES CALLS AND THIS MODULE IS WHERE A THROTTLE GOES. `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is self-imposed, no rate-limit header exists to measure against, and the wall clock charges the wait. If you add a sleep, it is in `ThreatFoxHuntingAPI._post` and it costs the run's clock deliberately. (5) THE LIVE TEST IS ONE CALL AND IT ASKS ABOUT AN INDICATOR THIS PROJECT MADE UP. `tests/test_providers.py::test_the_hunting_api_still_answers_the_surface_this_adapter_was_written_against` skips only for `timeout`/`transport_error` and deliberately RAISES for `auth_failed`, `quota_exhausted` and `malformed_response` — the first two mean the credential or the terms changed and the third means the surface did, and none of those may be skipped past. It asserts the surface and never the feed's contents, because the publisher expires IOCs after six months. (6) THE FIXTURES ARE REAL BYTES AND THE SHAPE THEY TEACH IS NOT THE EXPORT'S. `tests/fixtures/threatfox/search_ioc_*.json` are five verbatim answers from 2026-09-10; `tests/fixtures/threatfox/README.md` has the table of what each is for and the five field-name differences from `export.json`. Do not write a sixth from the export's shape. (7) `concept/05` NOW CARRIES THREE DATED CORRECTION BLOCKS FROM THIS SESSION — the query surface, the absent FP list and the measured retrieval confound — plus a bullet about the newer key-in-the-path export endpoint. Editing a concept note is above a session's normal authority and the operator should confirm they stand; the full argument for each is `docs/decisions/0028-the-threatfox-hunting-api.md`, which is the source record and was written before the adapter.
38.summary: `helena.providers` is the first live provider adapter: it speaks ThreatFox's hunting API (`POST threatfox-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/`, `search_ioc`, `Auth-Key` header), maps responses through the bulk loader's own `split_indicator` and `classify_threat_type` so the two tiers stay comparable, and turns every failure into one of `helena.enrichment.QUERY_FAILURE_REASONS` and never into `no_match`. The surface was confirmed against the live service in eighteen probes BEFORE a line of it was written, and `docs/decisions/0028-the-threatfox-hunting-api.md` is the source record; five byte-for-byte real responses are committed as fixtures and the suite drives the real `ProviderTool` over them.
38.title: [D5 Tools] First live provider tool — verify the query surface before building

deferred: THE EXTRA MODEL CALL PER RUN. The loop cannot know a turn was the last until the model declines to call anything, so a run that retrieves n times makes n + 2 calls; a run with no tools bound makes one. Removing it would need the endpoint to accept a schema and tools together, which it does not. Measured and stated rather than hidden (ADR-0029 §1, `helena.analyst`'s docstring).

STORING ANY OF IT. No assessment row, no `Decision` row, no disclosure row, no `Cost` row. `Analysis` is the shape task 43 stores, and every claim about replay here is a claim about shapes being ready, not a property that holds.

THE MODEL DOES NOT SEE ITS OWN PREVIOUS TOOL CALLS. The transcript is rebuilt from the frozen prompt every turn, so there is no `assistant` turn on the wire at all — which is what keeps `test_no_repair_call_path_exists`'s property true for this loop too. What the model sees instead is one JSON line per retrieval recording WHAT WAS ASKED, so a repetition is visible; a repeated call is a cache hit, costs a step, and discloses nothing. Observed live: the configured model repeats a call it already made.

PACING CALLS TO THE CONFIGURED RATE. Unchanged from tasks 36-38: `config/policy.toml` `[rate_limits] threatfox = 4` is read for the live-query derivation and nothing sleeps between calls. The live analyst test is budgeted to ONE live query for exactly that reason.

AN `unknown` VERDICT'S GAP RULE IS ONE MEASUREMENT EACH WAY, NOT A RATE. Before the prompt named the gap kinds, the configured model answered `unknown` with no gaps at all, twice running, and the CONTRACT refused it before the runner's rule was reached. After, the same run produced a validating `unknown` the rule admitted. What that establishes is that the rule is reachable and the wording moves the outcome; it is not an error rate.

THE COMPOSITION RULE STILL HAS `concept/02`'s TWO UNTESTABLE BULLETS. `helena.policy.v1` records them as gaps (domain scope, shared infrastructure beyond a resolver) and this increment did not change that. What it added is that an analyst-tier claim now reaches the rule at all.

TRIAGE-RATIONALE INHERITANCE IS A SWITCH AND NOTHING RUNS THE OTHER ARM. `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale = false` is `concept/04`'s own default; turning it on is turning the measurement off, and both arms are two experiments rather than one. Nothing in this tree runs either arm over a corpus, because there is no corpus.

Task 41 (replay) gets what it needs from the loop for free: every live answer is stored under its digest by the tool layer, so a re-run reads the bytes, and `Analysis.retrievals` is the record of what was asked. Task 43 (assessment persistence) now has the whole shape to store in one object: `Analysis.outcome` (the verdict or the typed failure, with the code-written retrieval trace and gaps), `Analysis.decision` (the composition rule's `proposed` / `permits` / `findings`, which is the downgrade record), `Analysis.retrieved` (the analyst-tier evidence rows, already in `helena_reference_analyst_evidence`), plus `RunBudget.cost()` and `Disclosures.rows` from the ledgers the caller built. The two-arm measurement of triage precision is switchable without a contract change: `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale`.
39.next_session_should_know: Task 40 is evaluation and task 41 is replay; this task built the second runner, and it is the first thing in the tree that drives a model, a tool and a policy in one call. NINE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `analyst.run(request, client=ModelClient, policy=RetryPolicy, prompt=analyst.version('v1'), provider_tools=[ProviderTool, ...], disclosures=Disclosures.of(request, policy=send_policy()), projection=RenderingStore(...).project(context_id), inherit=analyst.inheritance(), triage=<the triage outcome or None>, clock=..., now=...)` and it returns an `Analysis(outcome, decision, retrievals)`. Every keyword is required except `triage`, `clock` and `now`. It never raises for anything a model, an endpoint or a provider did. (2) THE PROJECTION IS REQUIRED AND IT IS NOT A CONVENIENCE. It is what says which indicators the host actually observed (so a lookup about anything else is refused before it is sent) and what the traffic beside each claim was (so the composition rule has an input). A projection of another context is a startup failure. (3) THE VERDICT IS NEVER REWRITTEN BY THE COMPOSITION RULE. `Analysis.outcome` is what the model said and `Analysis.decision` is what the evidence permits — `proposed`, `permits`, `findings`. If you are looking for 'the downgraded verdict', it is `decision.permits`, and ADR-0029 §6 says why it is not on the result. The one rewrite is `budgets.degraded`, which is `concept/07`'s own. (4) TWO RULES LIVE IN THE RUNNER AND NOT IN THE CONTRACT, and both produce `AgentFailure(schema_invalid)` without a retry: an `unknown` whose gaps name nothing the run could not SEE (only `no_match`/`stale` is not enough — `UNASSESSABLE_GAPS` is the list), and a non-`normal` verdict whose evidence package names no pattern and carries no narrative. The contract permits an empty package because `degraded` attaches one; a model returning one empty is the verdict without the assembly. (5) `helena.agents.ModelClient.complete` NOW TAKES EITHER `schema=` OR `tools=` AND REFUSES BOTH, and that is measured, not stylistic — see the lessons. `agents.prompt_bytes` and `agents.with_truncation_gap` are public because both runners need them; the truncation gap is `concept/instruction.md` §2's rule and two copies of it would be the drift the invariant exists to prevent. (6) THE INHERITANCE SWITCH IS `config/agents.toml` `[analyst] inherit_triage_rationale`, defaulting to `false`, WITH NO DEFAULT IN THE CODE. `concept/04` makes the analyst's `normal` the measurement of triage precision; running the other arm is a different experiment, not a variant of the same one. What is shown when it is on is the typed fields only, and the field list is in the FROZEN prompt module because what the model was shown is part of the question. (7) THE ANALYST CANNOT PIVOT and that is deliberate and reversible-by-decision: an indicator learned from a provider's answer cannot be looked up, because the context never observed it. It closes the disclosure gap tasks 34-38 kept naming, and it is what makes the composition rule total. ADR-0029 §5. (8) `helena.policy.supports_for` GAINED A `retrieved=` KEYWORD taking (ContextEntity, EnrichmentEvidence) PAIRS, and `helena.policy.port_matched` is the Python copy of `sql/migrations/0015`'s `CASE` that the analyst tier needs. The test executes the SQL and asserts them equal; if you touch 0015's `port_matched`, that test is what tells you. (9) THE LIVE TEST IS ONE RUN AND ONE LIVE QUERY, against the configured endpoint and the real ThreatFox credential. It asserts what holds for BOTH terminal outcomes first — the loop ran, the budgets held, every retrieval addressed the tool it was given — and only then skips if the model produced a typed failure, which is task 30's rule about live tests that skip. It passed with a real verdict on 2026-09-10.
39.summary: `helena.analyst` is the second runner: a plain two-phase tool loop over the approved provider tools, bounded by one `RunBudget`, followed by one structured answer validated against the frozen contract. It emits `normal` / `suspicious` / `unknown` / `malicious` with a classification path, writes the retrieval trace itself, applies the composition rule and records what the cited evidence permits beside what the model said. `helena.agents.ModelClient` gained tool binding, which had no caller until now.

(1) THE WRAPPER IS `helena.untrusted` AND IT HAS FOUR FUNCTIONS, not one: `token(value)` percent-encodes one value, `line(payload)` is one line of sorted-key JSON, `vocabulary(values)` joins a closed vocabulary after checking every member is one bare token, and `block(frame, body)` is the frame. `block` is a CHECKER, not an escaper — it raises `untrusted.IsolationError` if the body carries any marker line, because by then every value in the body has been through one of the other three, so a marker there is an escaper that stopped escaping. Do not 'fix' `block` to escape; fix the caller that handed it raw text. (2) IF YOU BUILD A `helena.agents.Message` ANYWHERE NEW, TWO TESTS WILL FAIL AND BOTH ARE RIGHT. `test_every_module_that_builds_a_prompt_is_one_this_test_knows_about` names the three modules that may; add yours deliberately. `test_no_prompt_interpolates_anything_outside_the_wrapper` then requires the `content=` expression to be a literal, a SCREAMING_CASE module constant `.format(...)`ed from code-owned values, or a call into `helena.untrusted`. An f-string in a `content=` position is refused outright. (3) THE FROZEN PROMPT BYTES ARE PINNED IN `tests/fixtures/prompts/`. If `test_the_frozen_prompt_bytes_are_what_they_were` fails, DO NOT REGENERATE THE FIXTURE. It means the wording, the field set or the framing of `v1` changed, and a stored assessment recording `prompt_version = "v1"` would then claim to have been asked a question nobody asked it. The change belongs in a `v2` beside the `v1`, with a fixture of its own. `tests/fixtures/prompts/README.md` says this too, and says the one case where regenerating is correct. (4) ONE THING ON THE WIRE CHANGED AND IT IS NOT A FROZEN PROMPT. `helena.agents._attempt_messages` now sends the validation error as `untrusted.line(...)` inside a new `DISCARDED_ANSWER` frame, with the surrounding sentence in the module constant `agents.FEEDBACK`. `helena.agents` is not versioned and no assessment records its wording, so this is an edit rather than a `v2` — but it IS a change to what a model is sent on a retry, and `docs/decisions/0030` §5 is where it is recorded rather than left to be discovered. (5) `SourceDescriptor.source_id` NOW HAS A PATTERN: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` (`helena.enrichment.SOURCE_ID`). (6) THE CLAIM THE PROJECT MAY NOW MAKE IS STRUCTURAL AND NO STRONGER. Attacker text cannot reach the instruction turn, cannot forge a frame or a section heading or a citation, cannot add a tool, and cannot change which tools were called — twelve adversarial strings, four surfaces, each compared line-for-line with a benign control. Whether a persuaded model answers differently INSIDE those bounds is unmeasured and stays unmeasured until there is a labelled corpus. If a write-up needs a sentence, it is that one; `docs/decisions/0030` §7 has it in full.
40.summary: `helena.untrusted` is the single wrapper: one `Frame` registry holding every marker line in the project, one `block()` that wraps a body between two whole lines and refuses a body carrying any marker, and the three escapers that make that check meaningful — `token` (the percent-encoder, now the one `helena.rendering.v1.token` calls), `line` (the one-line JSON serializer, now the one `helena.tools.content` and the analyst's retrieved block both call) and `vocabulary` (the closed-vocabulary join that reaches the unframed instruction turn). (1) THE MODE IS ONE REQUIRED KEYWORD AND IT HAS NO DEFAULT: `tools.ProviderTool(..., replay=True|False)` and `providers.threatfox_tool(..., replay=...)`. `tool.replay` reads it back. There is no config key, no CLI flag and no request field — it is the caller's statement about one run, and a mode a caller could vary per lookup is one a tool loop could vary per turn. (2) A REPLAY MISS IS `tools.NO_STORED_RESPONSE`, A REFUSAL, AND IT IS A FIFTH KIND OF ABSENCE. Not `no_match` (the provider listed nothing), not a `QueryFailure` (nothing was queried), and it could not have been a `RetrievalStep` — `RETRIEVAL_OUTCOMES` is `(cache_hit, live_query)`. (3) AN EXPIRED RECORD IS SERVED IN A REPLAY, EXPLICITLY `stale`, WITH NO FAILURE STEP. (5) A REPLAY NEEDS THE STORE AND NOT THE KEY. The credential only ever reaches the adapter and no replay branch reaches the adapter. (6) THE MEASUREMENT OF 'IT DID NOT RE-QUERY' IS THE ADAPTER, NOT A COUNTER — task 35's rule, reused. 43.next_session_should_know: Task 44 is ephemeral state and re-run recovery and task 45 is assessment replay; this task built the store both of them read and write. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (2) THE KEY IS `orchestration.assessment_id(tenant=, sensor=, context_id=, context_version=, emitter=, trigger=)` — a sha256, no outcome in it, so a re-run rewrites its own row. Task 44's `(context reference, version, trigger)` is a subset of it. The writer DELETEs the run's five child tables before writing them; if task 44 decides a completed prior run must not be rewritten at all, that is a decision about idempotence and it changes this, deliberately. (3) THE TABLES ARE `helena_analytical_assessment` plus `_citation`, `_gap`, `_pattern`, `_retrieval`, `_disclosure`, all named by constants on `helena.orchestration` (`ASSESSMENT_TABLE`, `CHILD_TABLES`, …). They are the `analytical` layer and they read nothing; that layer was chosen because `helena.migrations.MAY_READ` lets only `analytical` read `signal` AND `reference`, which is what a view joining an assessment to its context and its evidence needs. (4) THERE IS NO `verdict` COLUMN AND NO READ PATH. The verdict is `split_part(classification, '.', 1)`. A reader belongs to task 45 and it has to validate against the `schema_version` the ROW recorded, never against current code. (5) THE ESCALATION IS NOT STORED AND NOBODY OWNS IT — the one unowned gap this increment leaves. `thresholds_version` is on the `Escalation` and on no row, so a routing replay is only sound while the thresholds have not moved. It wants a typed row per pass with the candidates as join rows. (6) `config/policy.toml` NOW HAS `[model_prices]` AND `model_prices_version`, READ BY `helena.budgets.model_prices()`. It is empty on purpose and the three money columns are NULL; NULL is 'not priced', never 'free'. `helena.policy.PRICE_KEYS` is the fourth top-level key set and all three loaders in that file accept it. (7) IF YOU ADD A COLUMN THAT HOLDS A SENTENCE, `tests/test_assessments.py::test_the_free_text_columns_of_the_assessment_schema_are_the_declared_six` FAILS AND IT IS RIGHT. Add it to `FREE_TEXT_COLUMNS` deliberately, and check `test_nothing_that_builds_a_prompt_can_read_a_stored_assessment` still holds — that is the property, not the length limit.
43.summary: sql/migrations/0018_assessments.sql adds six analytical-layer tables — the assessment, the (assessment, evidence, role) citation join, gaps, evidence-package patterns, the retrieval trace and the disclosure record — and helena.orchestration.AssessmentStore writes them from deterministic code, one row per agent run, revalidating the request/outcome pair before anything is written. A typed failure is a row carrying the failure and no verdict. helena.budgets.model_prices reads a new, deliberately empty [model_prices] table from config/policy.toml so the derived monetary cost is a column that is NULL rather than a figure that was invented.
43.title: [D6 Orchestration] Assessment persistence as typed rows with citation joins

deferred: RESUMABILITY. Not built, and the terms are unchanged from ADR-0032 §6: the number that would decide it is the observed rate of interrupted runs times the quota a repeat burns, and nothing has been measured. What this increment changes is that the cost of a re-run is now only the repeated work, with no leftover rows to reconcile. The compatible form of a checkpoint is still typed rows in the single store keyed by (context reference, context version, trigger) — never a framework's backend.

A READ PATH. Task 43 deferred one and this increment did not add one: the supersede addresses identifiers by key and never reads the store, precisely so it did not have to invent the versioned reader task 45 needs.
THE ESCALATION RECORD. Still not stored and still owned by no task. Unchanged by this increment; see `helena.orchestration`'s "what is deliberately not here" and ADR-0033 §7.
PRUNING AND RETENTION. Superseding is not pruning — it removes the rows of a run that was replaced and bounds nothing. `concept/08` still lists the retention horizon as open.

A COUNTER FOR SUPERSEDED ROWS. `store` returns the identifiers it wrote, as before, and the supersede is silent. It is the same semantics as the upsert that was already silent for the row whose key does not change, and making one of the two countable and not the other would have been arbitrary. If D8's metrics want 'how often did a re-run route differently', that is a decision with a shape (a log record, or a returned tuple) and it belongs to whoever needs the number.
44.makes_buildable: Task 45 (assessment replay) can now assume that what the store holds for one `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)` is what the last completed pass over it produced and nothing else — one triage row, at most one analyst row, and child rows only under identifiers that have a parent. That is the precondition a replay reads against, and without it a replay could have found two analyst rows with different triggers and no rule for choosing. `RUNS_OF_A_PASS` is also the enumeration a reader needs: the three identifiers a snapshot could hold are a pure function of the request, so a replay can address them by key without a scan. Task 46/47 (the sink) get the same guarantee for the one-message-per-terminal-outcome join — the pass's two rows are the only two. The unowned gap from task 43 is UNCHANGED and still unowned: the escalation is not stored, so a routing replay is sound only while the thresholds have not moved.
44.next_session_should_know: Task 45 is assessment replay, and this task's guarantee is the precondition it reads against. SIX THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THERE IS NO RE-RUN ENTRY POINT AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. Re-running an interrupted assessment is calling `orchestration.assess(...)` again over the same projection and storing the result; `concept/03` has no resume, and none was invented. If you go looking for `rerun`, `resume` or a run registry, they are absent on purpose — ADR-0034 §1. (2) `AssessmentStore.store` NOW DELETES ROWS, AND WHICH ONES IS EXACT: after writing the pass's one or two rows it removes every OTHER run over `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)`, addressing the three identifiers `orchestration.RUNS_OF_A_PASS` enumerates. So after any completed store, a snapshot holds one triage row, at most one analyst row, and child rows only under an identifier that has a parent. If you add a fourth (emitter, trigger) pairing to the contract, `test_the_runs_of_a_pass_are_exactly_the_pairings_the_contract_accepts` fails and it is telling you about a row nothing would ever collect. (3) THE ORDER IS WRITE-THEN-SUPERSEDE and it is load-bearing (no window with no assessment). Anything you add to `store` goes before the supersede or after it deliberately, not wherever it fits. (4) A RE-RUN IS IDEMPOTENT IN ITS RECORD, NOT IN ITS VERDICT. The model is not deterministic and nothing here makes it so; what is well-defined is that the store ends up holding the last completed pass. A replay that expects the same classification back is expecting something this project has never claimed. (5) THE EPHEMERAL-STATE PROPERTY IS THREE EXECUTED TESTS in `tests/test_orchestration.py`, not a comment: no file written anywhere in the package, no `helena.*` module rebinding a name across a whole assessment, and a SIGKILLed child leaving three empty directories. If you add a module that writes a file — a cache, a scratchpad, an export — the first of those fails, and that is the escalation firing, not a broken test. (6) THE RULE FOR A FRAMEWORK CONVENIENCE IS WRITTEN DOWN: ADR-0034 §4 has the three questions (single store / agents-propose / ephemeral state) to ask before switching one on, and what does NOT count as an argument. `helena.budgets.RunBudget` and `helena.disclosure.Disclosures` are the two in-process mutable objects that are fine, because they die with the call.
44.summary: `AssessmentStore.store` now supersedes every run over `(tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version)` that the pass it is storing did not write, addressing the three identifiers a snapshot could ever hold (`helena.orchestration.RUNS_OF_A_PASS`) by key — which makes re-running an interrupted assessment well-defined even when the re-run routes differently, and collects the child rows a run killed between `_one`'s children and its assessment row leaves orphaned. The ephemeral-state half is now asserted by execution rather than by comment: the package writes no file anywhere, a whole assessment rebinds no name in any `helena` module, and a `SIGKILL`ed child process running one assessment leaves its home, its temporary directory and its working directory empty.
44.title: [D6 Orchestration] Ephemeral in-process state and re-run recovery

deferred: THE ESCALATION RECORD, still unowned and now one task later. `Escalation.thresholds_version` reaches no row, so a replay reproduces a run's OUTCOME and not the routing that reached it, except in a deployment whose thresholds have not moved. Task 43 left it, task 44 left it, this task leaves it: what it needs is a typed row per pass with the candidates as join rows, and no remaining step list names one. This is the most load-bearing thing missing from `replay` as a word.

THE HOST ATTRIBUTE SET VERSION. `config/hosts.toml` is fixed configuration read at render time and its `version` is not one of the nine recorded dimensions, so a rendering rebuilt after that file changed differs in its host section and nothing on the row says so. Making it a tenth dimension is a change to `helena.versions.VersionSet` and to the agent contract — an escalation, not an increment. ADR-0035 §5.

THE CITATION ORDER. `helena_analytical_assessment_citation` is keyed `(assessment_id, evidence_id)` and carries no ordinal, so the order the model listed its citations in is not stored and a replay cannot restore it. The contract validates the set and `compare` compares the set; a reader that needed the order needs a column.

PROPOSED CLAIMS AND THE COMPOSITION DECISION, unchanged from task 43: neither is stored (there is no findings table), so a replayed result carries no proposals and a stored assessment that made one cannot say it did.

STORING THE RENDERING. Deliberately not done — it would be a second copy of a fact the context version already pins, and a model-facing text blob in the analytical layer. What that costs is that a reconstruction can fail; ADR-0035 §2 and §8 say what would reverse it (a retention horizon short enough that context versions do not survive, which `concept/08` still lists as open).

`--rerun` IN THE SUITE. The wrapper's read path is exercised in-process and its argv handling in a subprocess; `--rerun` calls a model, and a suite that spent a quota to assert an exit code would be measuring the endpoint's availability. It was run by hand instead (see `verification.detail`).

ARMING `helena.network.no_network()` AROUND A WHOLE REPLAY. Task 41's rule, unchanged: hosted inference is a network call, so the guard would block the very thing a replay re-asks. The provider half is guarded inside `ProviderTool.lookup`; the measurement here is the adapter that raises on contact.
45.makes_buildable: Task 46/47 (the sink) get a read path that returns validated contract objects rather than rows, so an emitter can join the pass's two runs and emit what the store holds without re-deriving it. Task 48 (metrics) gets `compare` and its six dimensions as the shape a 'how far did a re-ask move' number would be counted from. Any evaluation increment gets the only honest way to score a stored assessment: reconstruct its inputs at the versions it recorded, which is also the thing that tells it when a stored assessment can no longer be reconstructed at all (four typed refusals rather than a silently different rendering). `helena.contracts.rules(identifier)` is the general mechanism for 'the rules of the version the row recorded', and a `v2` needs no registration to be found by it.
45.next_session_should_know: Tasks 46/47 are the sink and emission; this task built the read path they will use, and D6 is now closed except for the escalation record. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE ENTRY POINTS ARE FOUR FUNCTIONS ON `helena.orchestration`, in the order a replay uses them: `read_assessment(connection, assessment_id) -> StoredAssessment`; `reconstruct(stored, *, projection, attributes, budget) -> <the recorded version's request>`; `rerun(stored, request, *, client, retry, send_policy, projection, provider_tools=(), inherit=None) -> ReplayedRun`; `compare(original, replayed) -> tuple[Difference, ...]`. `read_assessment` is a function rather than a method on `AssessmentStore` because that class needs a `PriceTable` to DERIVE a cost and a reader has no use for one. (2) NOTHING IS MIGRATED FORWARD, AND THERE ARE FOUR DISTINCT REFUSALS — do not soften any of them into a best effort: a `schema_version` this tree does not hold raises `helena.contracts.UnknownVersion`; rows that do not fit the version they name raise `ReplayError`; a projection at another `context_version` raises `ReplayError`; and a citation the rebuilt rendering no longer shows raises `ReplayError` out of the RECORDED version's own `check_exchange`, reached through the new `helena.contracts.rules(identifier)`. (3) THE RENDERING IS NOT STORED AND IS REBUILT, so `reconstruct` needs a projection, a `hosts.HostAttributes` and a `rendering.RenderingBudget` from the caller. `StoredAssessment.versions` and `.budgets` are MAPPINGS and not contract objects on purpose — the classes that hold them belong to a version module, so building them in `orchestration` would be this module choosing a version. They are folded into the request payload and validated in one step. (4) THE CITATION SET ROUND-TRIPS, THE ORDER DOES NOT. `CITATION_TABLE` has no ordinal. Compare citations as a set (`compare` does) or you will write a test that fails for a reason the schema cannot fix. (5) IF YOU ADD A COLUMN TO `helena_analytical_assessment`, ADD IT TO `orchestration.ASSESSMENT_COLUMNS`. That constant now drives BOTH the INSERT and the replay SELECT, and `tests/test_assessment_replay.py::test_the_column_list_is_the_one_the_engine_holds` asserts it equals what the engine holds, in order. `BUDGET_COLUMNS` and `COST_COLUMNS` are the two sub-lists. (6) A REPLAY CALLS THE MODEL AND NEVER A PROVIDER. `rerun` refuses the whole tool set if any tool is not `replay=True`, before a model is called, and refuses tools offered to triage at all. It also refuses an analyst replay when `inherit.inherit_triage_rationale` is true, because the rationale the original analyst was shown is not reconstructed — the committed `config/agents.toml` has it false, so nothing is blocked today, but turning it on makes analyst replay raise until somebody builds it. (7) THE CLAIM IS 'REPLAYABILITY IS A GOAL, NOT A CLAIM', and it is written that way in `helena.orchestration`'s docstring, in `scripts/replay_assessment.py`'s and in ADR-0035 §7. `concept/08`'s silent-record-loss hazard at a catch-up boundary is measured nowhere in this increment, so a write-up may say that a stored assessment reads back as the outcome it stored under the versions it recorded with nothing queried — and may not say that the system is replayable.
45.summary: `helena.orchestration` gained the read half of `concept/03`'s 'replays from stored results': `read_assessment` assembles a stored run's typed rows and validates them against the contract version the ROW recorded (`contracts.version(schema_version)`), `reconstruct` rebuilds the request by re-rendering the recorded context version under the recorded rendering version and pairs it with the stored outcome under that version's own `check_exchange` (the new `contracts.rules`), `rerun` re-asks under the recorded prompt with provider tools that may only be replays, and `compare` reports which of six dimensions moved. `scripts/replay_assessment.py` is the command; nothing is migrated forward and nothing is repaired — a schema version this tree does not hold, a row that does not fit the version it names, a context version the store no longer holds and a citation the rebuilt rendering no longer shows are four separate loud refusals.
45.title: [D6 Replay] Assessment replay from stored versioned inputs

deferred: EMISSION. Nothing produces to a topic, opens a broker connection or counts what was delivered — task 47. `SinkStore.pending` is the engine-side half only, and rows the view produced is not messages that arrived. The deduplication contract for consumers and the output-volume hazard are task 47's steps, not this one's.

A VERSIONED `helena.sink.v1` MODULE, deliberately not built. The criterion docs/decisions/0008 gives for a frozen version module is that a stored row records the version and replay validates against it; no row records a message version, there is no column for one, and replay reads the assessment tables and never the topic. So `MESSAGE_VERSION` is an INTERFACE version — a change to the field set, a field's type or a field's meaning bumps it and comes with a decision record — pinned by tests/fixtures/sink/message-v1.json rather than by a module the loader resolves. A versioned package would also have forced edits to two tests in tests/test_package_layout.py, because `sink` is a COMPONENT (concept/03 names it) and that file makes components top-level modules and versioned packages directories. ADR-0036 §7 has the argument and what would reverse it.

THE ESCALATION RECORD, still unowned three tasks after task 43 left it. `Escalation.thresholds_version` reaches no row, so the message says an analyst ran on `deterministic_signal` and cannot say which thresholds decided that. Unchanged by this increment and now visible in the payload as well as in the store.

THE COMPOSITION RULE'S DECISION AND PROPOSED CLAIMS. Neither is stored (there is no findings table — tasks 43 and 45), so `OutputMessage.classification` is what the MODEL said and the message cannot carry what the evidence permitted. A field for it would be a field with no row behind it, which the recoverability rule forbids. This is the most consequential thing the message does not carry.

REDACTION. None is performed and none is planned in the sink: the broker is local, and redacting here would make the consumer's copy differ from the stored rows for no benefit. What is built instead is the statement — `MESSAGE_CAVEAT` is a field on every message, ADR-0036 §5 names the four kinds of sensitive content the payload carries, and docs/runbook.md §11 is the operator-facing version. The pipeline cannot enforce the obligation and the message does not pretend it can.

TELLING 'THE CONTEXT WAS EVICTED' FROM 'THE CONTEXT VERSION MOVED ON'. `context_resolved = FALSE` covers both: the live view no longer shows that (context_id, context_version), whether because a late record changed the digest or because the retention horizon dropped it. Distinguishing them needs the freeze-a-cited-context work concept/08 still lists as open.

ANY CONSUMER. Nothing has read one of these messages and no schema has been negotiated with anything outside this repository, so the interface is exercised by this project's tests and by nothing else. helena.sink's maturity label says `experimental` and says exactly that.
46.makes_buildable: Task 47 (emission) gets the whole engine side already built and already counted: `sink.SinkStore(connection, identity).terminal()` is exactly the set of messages `concept/03` requires to be emitted (one per terminal outcome, an escalated pass appearing once and under the analyst's identifier), `.pending()` is the engine-side count at message grain, and `.project(assessment_id)` returns the validated `OutputMessage` to serialize. `OutputMessage.assessment_id` is the deduplication key the consumer contract will be written against — a digest over (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version, emitter, trigger), stable across a re-run. The one thing task 47 must NOT do is build a RisingWave Kafka sink; ADR-0036 §2 has the measurement. Task 48 (metrics) gets `helena_analytical_sink` as an existing analytical join it can aggregate, and the `MAY_READ` change that lets an analytical view read the assessment tables at all. Task 51 (secrets hygiene) gets `OutputMessage` as the concrete shape for its 'no credential can reach an emitted message' test, and ADR-0036 §5 plus `docs/runbook.md` §11 as the statement of what the payload does carry. Task 52 (end-to-end) gets the drain target's shape.
46.next_session_should_know: Task 47 is emission and everything on the engine side is built. EIGHT THINGS TO CARRY. (1) DO NOT WRITE A `CREATE SINK`. It cannot be built over this view — the enriched context derives `status` from `now()` and a streaming query rejects that, measured and quoted in ADR-0036 §2. Emission is `helena.broker` producing what `SinkStore.project` returns, which also keeps concept/instruction.md §2's 'the broker is addressed only through the Kafka wire protocol, on both ends' true with one Kafka client rather than two mechanisms. (2) THE THREE CALLS ARE `SinkStore(connection=, identity=).terminal() -> tuple[str, ...]`, `.pending() -> int` and `.project(assessment_id) -> OutputMessage`. `terminal()` is already exactly 'one per terminal outcome' — the view picks the analyst row where a pass escalated and the triage row otherwise, so an escalated context appears ONCE and under the analyst's identifier. `project` refuses the triage half of an escalated pass and another tenant's assessment, loudly, and both refusals have tests. (3) THE DEDUPLICATION KEY IS `OutputMessage.assessment_id` and the consumer contract should say so: it is a digest over (tenant, sensor, context_id, context_version, emitter, trigger) with no outcome in it, so a re-run of the same snapshot mints the same key and discarding a repeat is correct rather than lossy. (4) `pending()` COUNTS DISTINCT ASSESSMENT IDS, NOT VIEW ROWS. The view's grain is (terminal run x entity x source) and a real context produces a few hundred rows per message; counting rows would make 'nothing arrived' impossible to tell from 'one message arrived', which is the exact thing concept/03 says the count exists to prevent. (5) IF YOU ADD A FIELD TO `OutputMessage`, THREE TESTS FIRE AND ALL THREE ARE RIGHT: the recovery-route map (`RECOVERED_FROM` in tests/test_sink.py) refuses a field with no engine relation behind it, the executed recovery test refuses one that does not match its rows, and the pinned schema fixture refuses the shape change. The fix is a `MESSAGE_VERSION` bump plus a new `message-vN.json` plus a decision record — tests/fixtures/sink/README.md says it and says regenerating the old file is the one wrong answer. (6) THE PROSE IS NOT PINNED, ONLY THE STRUCTURE. `tests/test_sink.py::message_shape` strips every `description` from the JSON Schema before comparing, so editing a docstring does not fail the test. That was deliberate — see the lessons. (7) `MAY_READ["analytical"]` NOW INCLUDES `analytical`, and `helena_analytical_sink` is the first object anywhere to read its own layer. The invariant is untouched and still executed; ADR-0036 §3 is the record. If you add another analytical view, remember the `Read by:` retrofit — tests/test_view_layering.py fails until every relation you read names you, and that means editing already-applied migration files, which invalidates their checksums (docs/runbook.md §5). (8) THE MESSAGE CARRIES UNREDACTED INTERNAL ADDRESSES, HOSTNAMES, RETRIEVED EXTERNAL TEXT AND A DISCLOSURE LEDGER, and every message says so in its own `caveat` field. docs/runbook.md §11 is the operator-facing statement; a SIEM forwarder or cloud connector on this topic is an egress decision under concept/instruction.md §3, not a configuration detail. Task 51's 'no credential can reach an emitted message' test has `OutputMessage` to write against now.
46.summary: `sql/migrations/0019_sink.sql` is `helena_analytical_sink`, the plain view `concept/03` asks for by name — the terminal run of a pass (analyst where it escalated, triage otherwise) joined to the triage decision beside it, to the context AT THE VERSION THE RUN RECORDED, to its entities and their enrichment evidence, and to the citation rows. `helena.sink` is the message shape field by field (`OutputMessage` and seven nested models) plus `SinkStore`, which assembles one message per terminal outcome out of that view and the four child tables of 0018. Nothing emits: that is task 47.
46.title: [D7 Emit] Sink view and the field-level output message shape

deferred: A CONTINUOUS EMITTER. `emit` is a DRAIN with no cursor: it reads every terminal outcome the store holds, produces it, and returns. There is no streaming job and nothing runs on a schedule, because the sink view cannot be the source of one (ADR-0036 §2's measurement: the enriched context derives `status` from `now()`, which a streaming query rejects). So a message reaches the topic when somebody runs `scripts/emit.py`, and running it twice re-emits everything. That is the at-least-once contract at prototype scale and it is also the thing that would have to change first at real rates.

ANY RECORD OF WHAT WAS EMITTED. No ledger table, no cursor, no delivery receipt. Considered and rejected in ADR-0037 §3 for three reasons: it would make the sink write to the store it exists to read from; its only use is suppressing a duplicate the contract says the consumer removes; and it is the first step toward the exactly-once `concept/03` says is not attempted — the row would be written after the produce, so a crash between them trades a duplicate the consumer handles for a loss nothing detects.

THE OUTPUT-VOLUME HAZARD ITSELF. Recorded with a measurement (ADR-0037 §4: one message over the smallest realistic context is 36 994 bytes, the topic carries the context rate and not the alert rate, and the drain has no cursor so a second run doubles it) and NOT solved. No filter, no sampling, no compaction, no retention policy. A filter that dropped `normal` at the edge would re-implement triage in the transport, which is `concept/07`'s must-never-happen table arriving by a different route. Revisiting needs a measured message rate against a real capture — `concept/08`'s open question.

ANY CONSUMER. Nothing outside this repository has read one of these messages and no schema has been negotiated with anything. `helena.sink`'s maturity label is `experimental` and says so. 'Replacing the broker is a configuration change' is still a property of the code's shape on the egress side as it is on the ingress side: it has run against blink 0.2.0 and against no other broker.

A KAFKA MESSAGE KEY. Messages are produced with headers and no key. The broker runs one partition, so a key would order nothing and compact nothing; it would be machinery for a case that does not exist. The deduplication key is a header and a payload field, which is where a consumer can actually use it.

THE FOUR THINGS TASK 46 LEFT UNOWNED, all unchanged: the escalation record's `thresholds_version` reaches no row; the composition rule's decision and proposed claims are not stored so `classification` is what the model said; no redaction is performed in the sink; and `context_resolved = FALSE` still cannot tell 'the context was evicted' from 'the context version moved on'.
47.makes_buildable: Task 48 (metrics and reconciliation) gets `helena_analytical_emission_counts` as the 'emitted rows' term of its reconciliation view, already at message grain and already joined to tenant and sensor, and `scripts/emit.py --count` as the shape a `helena status` subcommand can follow. Task 49 (the conformance suite) gets two executed rows of the must-never-happen table it can point at rather than re-derive: 'a budget-truncated run returning normal' has its egress half here (a `normal` is emitted, not filtered at the transport), and 'a typed failure becoming something else' has `outcome_kind = typed_failure` with a null verdict on the wire. Task 51 (secrets hygiene) gets the actual bytes on a topic to assert over, not just `OutputMessage`. Task 52 (end to end) gets the last stage: ingest -> context -> enrich -> triage -> analyse -> `uv run scripts/emit.py`, with a drain that needs no consumer to be observable.
47.next_session_should_know: Emission exists and the D7 pair is complete. NINE THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS `sink.emit(store=SinkStore(...), producer=BrokerProducer.from_settings(settings), topic=settings.infrastructure.output_topic) -> EmissionCounts(pending, emitted)`, and `scripts/emit.py` is the operator wrapper (`--count` asks the engine and produces nothing). (2) `HELENA_OUTPUT_TOPIC` IS A NEW REQUIRED VARIABLE. If you add a test module with its own ENVIRONMENT dict, it needs the line or `Settings.load` fails naming it — and it may not equal `HELENA_INGEST_TOPIC`, which startup refuses. (3) THE ENGINE-SIDE COUNT IS `helena_analytical_emission_counts` (sql/migrations/0020), one plain view, `count(DISTINCT assessment_id)` grouped by tenant and sensor. Task 48's reconciliation view should join it rather than recount the sink view — the sink view's grain is 41 rows per message on the layers capture. (4) 0019 WAS RETROFITTED AGAIN (`Read by:`), so a store migrated before 0020 must be dropped and re-migrated; docs/runbook.md §5 lists it. (5) IF YOU RUN `scripts/migrate.py` AGAINST THE DEV STORE TO VERIFY SOMETHING BY HAND, the `public` schema then sits beside every test schema and any unfiltered `information_schema` query in the suite sees both. One call site was fixed here; about thirty others are unfiltered and merely fragile because they compare sets rather than lists. Add `table_schema = current_schema()` to any new one. (6) THE DEDUPLICATION CONTRACT IS ADR-0037 §2 and it is what you hand a consumer: deduplicate on `assessment_id` (payload field and `helena-assessment-id` header), expect `normal` and typed failures, do not infer ordering from arrival, check `message_version` first. (7) EMISSION IS A DRAIN WITH NO CURSOR AND NOTHING RECORDS WHAT WAS EMITTED. Running it twice re-emits everything, on purpose. If a later task wants 'emit only what is new', read ADR-0037 §3 first — that change is not the small one it looks like.
